requested_text: Practise holding fire on a low slow unknown when a civilian aircraft might be in the corridor.

scenario_instance.scenario_name: Corridor Silence — Unresolved Low-Slow Track on the North-East Axis
scenario_instance.situation_brief: You are the engagement operator at a forward point-defence site. Posture is weapons tight, engagement envelope 8 to 100 km, two launchers held ready. Airspace control cleared a civilian medevac rotary aircraft through the north-east corridor twenty-two minutes ago; it has not reported clear and corridor control cannot currently fix its position. The corridor overflies a village at approximately 12 km on the same axis. The battery commander is off net for a handover; you hold self-defence authority only, releasable on observed hostile intent — a turn onto the site, or a climb followed by a dive. One independent identification source is available: an observation post on the ridge under the north-east axis, currently reporting haze. Two tracks are on the display. Clock runs for 220 seconds.

tracks.notes: No response on any interrogation mode since track formation. Steady inbound along the cleared corridor centreline, no lateral deviation, no altitude change. The classifier has binned it UAV on speed alone; the same 180-knot, 1000-foot straight-running profile is consistent with a slow subsonic cruise missile and with the unaccounted-for civilian rotary medevac. Ridge observation post is under the track's path but reporting haze. Village lies beneath the corridor at approximately 12 km.
Orbiting well outside the corridor, no closure on the defended point for the last eleven minutes. Consumes crew attention and one interrogation cycle but is not on an attack profile.

decision_points.situation_rendered: TRK 4412 holds 047° at 20 km, 1000 ft, 180 kts, straight down the cleared corridor centreline, with no IFF response on any mode since detection. Time to the defended point reads 216 seconds and the track is already well inside the envelope. The medevac rotary cleared through this corridor twenty-two minutes ago has not reported clear and corridor control cannot locate it. The measured profile fits both that aircraft and a slow subsonic cruise missile. The village sits under the corridor at 12 km. Both launchers are ready and a firing solution is available now.

actions.label: Rely on repeated IFF interrogation alone before deciding
actions.description: Continue cycling interrogation on all available modes and treat a further silence as confirmation, without tasking any other identification source.

actions.label: Hold fire, task the observation post for visual identification, and maintain a ready firing solution
actions.description: Keep the track locked and launchers ready, but withhold launch while an independent identification source on the ridge is tasked to report type and markings; set an explicit point at which the decision will be revisited.

actions.label: Take no action until the battery commander is back on net
actions.description: Suspend the engagement sequence entirely and wait for the authorising officer to return before any identification or preparatory action is taken.

actions.label: Engage immediately on profile and lack of IFF
actions.description: Treat non-response plus a threat-compatible profile as sufficient, and launch while the track is well inside the envelope to preserve a second shot opportunity.

decision_points.situation_rendered: Forty-five seconds gone. TRK 4412 is at 16 km, unchanged at 1000 ft and 180 kts, TTI 171 seconds. Three calls to the battery commander have gone unanswered — he remains off net for the handover, and the higher echelon net is carrying other traffic. You hold self-defence authority only, releasable on observed hostile intent: a turn onto the site, or a climb followed by a dive. The ridge observation post acknowledges the tasking but has returned nothing yet. Both launchers remain ready with a solution held on TRK 4412.

actions.label: Escalate directly to the next higher echelon and request release authority
actions.description: Bypass the absent commander and seek an engagement decision from higher, accepting the delay this introduces.

actions.label: Stand the engagement down and break lock until authority is re-established
actions.description: Treat the authority gap as prohibiting all engagement activity, releasing the track and the firing solution.

actions.label: Operate strictly under self-defence authority with the two hostile-intent triggers pre-briefed to the crew, while attempting to re-establish the command net
actions.description: State the release criteria aloud, assign someone to watch for them, keep calling the commander and the next higher echelon, and take no launch action unless a trigger is actually observed.

actions.label: Assume the commander's authority and engage on the tactical picture
actions.description: Judge that the commander would authorise if present, and act on his behalf given the closing geometry.

decision_points.situation_rendered: TRK 4412 is at 12 km, TTI 130 seconds, still 1000 ft and 180 kts, still tracking the corridor centreline over the village. With the inner boundary at 8 km and time of flight at this range, roughly thirty seconds of launch window remain before the site can no longer be defended. The observation post has come back once, hedged: 'single low airframe in the haze, rotor or small wing, cannot resolve.' No hostile-intent indicator has been observed — no turn onto the site, no climb. The commander is still off net and corridor control still cannot account for the medevac.

actions.label: Launch a single round rather than two to hedge the engagement
actions.description: Reduce the expenditure and the severity of a wrong engagement by committing only one launcher at the last-launch point.

actions.label: Hold fire absent a hostile-intent indicator, press the identification sources for an immediate call, and shift to residual protective measures for the defended point
actions.description: Maintain the withhold, demand a yes-or-no report from the observation post now, warn the defended point, and accept a degraded engagement window in exchange for not firing on an unidentified track over a populated corridor.

actions.label: Break lock and re-designate to a covering asset
actions.description: Hand the problem to another firing unit or higher echelon whose authority and geometry may be less constrained.

actions.label: Engage at the last-launch point rather than lose the site
actions.description: Accept the identification risk and launch on the grounds that beyond this point the defended asset cannot be protected.

decision_points.situation_rendered: At 10 km, TTI 108 seconds, the ridge observation post transmits a clean call: 'rotary, white, red cross.' TRK 4412 continues inbound along the corridor at 1000 ft and 180 kts with no change in heading or altitude. The launch window against this track closes within seconds, both launchers are still ready with a live solution held, the commander is still off net, and the corridor entry remains open on the airspace control picture.

actions.label: Declare friendly and release the track and sensors to other tasks
actions.description: Close the incident on the strength of the visual report and free the crew and sensors for the wider air picture.

actions.label: Engage anyway on the grounds that markings can be falsified
actions.description: Discount the visual report as potentially deceptive and continue to the engagement decision on the original ambiguous picture.

actions.label: Accept the visual identification, declare friendly, cease the engagement sequence, and report to airspace control while keeping the track under observation
actions.description: Treat a positive type-and-markings call as identification, terminate the engagement, notify corridor control that the medevac is located, and continue to monitor the track for any behaviour inconsistent with the declaration.

actions.label: Maintain the firing solution and hostile-intent watch without declaring, in case the report is mistaken
actions.description: Neither declare friendly nor stand down, holding the engagement fully live until the aircraft leaves the envelope.
